summary.headline: MARA and EIX persist RED (both standing, thesis-confirmed structural risks, not day-to-day price flags). NVDA's blowout Q2 FY2027 print (revenue $96.22B, +106% YoY; FY2028 growth guided to +70%) was the day's dominant catalyst -- NVDA +8.77% added roughly $442B in market value (2nd-largest single-day gain ever) and lifted the broader AI-infra complex (FTNT +9.61% to a fresh 52-week high on continuing Q2 momentum, CRDO +6.15%, TSM +2.24%, LRCX +1.75%), while a wave of BTC/crypto strength lifted MARA +5.61%, COIN +4.99%, HOOD +1.20% -- AEM, HOOD, COIN, and ATAT/HUT (already green) all resolve their prior AMBER flags on calm-to-positive price action with no new negative catalysts. Two new items: SUPV -4.22% is the book's largest single decliner with no same-day tier-1 catalyst found, but it directly matches its own recurring Argentine-macro/credit-quality key_risk despite a genuinely improving Q2 (return to profit, NIM expansion) -- capped AMBER. MRVL beat Q2 revenue/EPS estimates and raised its FY2028 guide to ~$18B (above its own thesis's $16.5B key_risk threshold) but still sold off (-8% premarket per CNBC, settling at -1.56% for the session) as the Google custom-silicon partnership commentary underwhelmed elevated Street hopes -- a 'sell the news' reaction worth flagging on its own, kept AMBER given the modest settled move. New AMBER: a broad, catalyst-less Dividend-sleeve pullback (SYK/ABT/PCAR/TOL/GPC/ATO/CL/NEE, -0.9% to -2.3%) against a firm broader tape (SPY +0.68%, QQQ +1.39%) reads as rotation into AI/growth on the NVDA print, not sector-specific stress. CWAN roster-integrity bug hits its 62nd consecutive day, still three open unmerged duplicate PRs (#11, #12, #14) -- needs a human merge. SPY sits ~19.36% above its one active support (645.80), not in play. EIX's Aug-31 wildfire-liability legislative deadline is now 3 days out with no bill passed -- the most time-critical item on the board heading into next week.

flags.headline: +5.61% today, a normal BTC-correlated rebound -- but the standing structural risk (GAAP losses, BTC leverage) is unchanged
flags.detail: MARA +5.61% to $11.85 (prev close $11.23), tracking a broad crypto-sector rally alongside COIN (+4.99%) and HOOD (+1.20%) -- unlike 8/27's decoupling, today's move is BTC-correlated as expected for a leveraged Bitcoin-mining name. This is not a resolution of the standing flag: MARA's August 6 Q2 print showed a $611M net loss with a $343M Bitcoin mark-to-market hit, the company carries $850M in convertible debt, and its entire financial performance remains a leveraged derivative of Bitcoin price with no demonstrated crypto-independent profitability. This flag has been held RED continuously since the Q2 miss (first_seen 2026-08-11) through both down days and rallies -- it tracks the standing thesis risk, not the daily price tape.
flags.thesis_link: Matches MARA key_risk: 'Revenue concentration in Bitcoin mining means MARA's financial performance is essentially a leveraged derivative of Bitcoin price -- the company has no proven ability to generate profits independent of crypto market conditions' and 'Persistent GAAP losses ($1.3B in Q1 2026 alone)... create existential risk if crypto enters a prolonged downturn and the company cannot service its $850M convertible debt obligations.'

flags.headline: Calm today (-1.14%) but the Aug-31 legislative deadline is now only 3 days out -- still no bill passed
flags.detail: EIX -1.14% to $73.67 (prev close $74.52). Confirmed via this run's search: California's legislative session deadline of August 31 is now 3 days away, and no wildfire-liability reform bill has passed despite Governor Newsom's last-minute push (reported as recently as this week). CEO Pedro Pizarro's public warning stands -- failure to pass credit-supportive reform would likely push SCE's already-lowest-investment-grade S&P rating into junk territory. If the legislature adjourns without a deal, Newsom could call a special session, but that would not avert the immediate credit-rating exposure. This is the most time-critical item on the board: the next scheduled run should land on or just after the deadline itself.
flags.thesis_link: Matches EIX key_risk: 'Elevated debt-to-equity of 216% amplifies financial risk from future wildfire events, adverse rate case outcomes, or rising interest rates... a single catastrophic fire in SCE's territory could create material liability.'

evidence.source: Seeking Alpha -- 'Edison falls 5% after warning that California legislature may not act by August 31 deadline'

flags.headline: Beat Q2 revenue/EPS and raised FY2028 guide above its own thesis threshold -- but sold off anyway on underwhelming detail versus Street hype
flags.detail: Marvell's Q2 FY2027 results, reported after close 8/27, beat: record revenue of $2.739B (+37% YoY, $39M above guidance midpoint), non-GAAP EPS $0.94, Data Center revenue growth accelerating to 46% YoY. The company also raised its FY2028 revenue outlook to ~$18B, above the $16.5B level its own key_risk had flagged as the bar to clear. Despite the beat-and-raise, shares fell as much as 8% in premarket (CNBC) before settling at -1.56% for the session ($238.97, prev close $245.115) -- CNBC attributes the reaction to limited detail on the up-to-$12.2B Google custom-silicon partnership that the Street had been pricing in ahead of the print. A 'sell the news' reaction on fundamentals that clear the thesis's own bar is itself informative: it confirms just how much execution premium is embedded in the 53x forward multiple the thesis already flagged. Kept AMBER rather than resolved, given the settled-session decline and the valuation-compression risk remaining live; not escalated to RED given the modest actual move.
flags.thesis_link: Matches MRVL key_risk: 'Forward P/E of 53.3x and trailing P/E of 83.5x after a ~150% stock price surge embed extraordinary growth expectations -- any miss against the $16.5B FY2028 revenue target or moderation in hyperscaler AI capex would trigger severe multiple compression.' Results actually beat this target, yet the stock still sold off -- a valuation-premium story rather than a fundamentals story.

evidence.source: CNBC -- 'Marvell stock tumbles 8% as outlook underwhelms despite Google deal'
Marvell Technology Investor Relations -- Q2 FY2027 financial results
